security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI HSM suspend handler saves/restores M-mode CSR context but does not include mtval3; when M-mode memory tagging is enabled (mseccfg.MT_MODE != 00), the tag-mismatch faulting virtual address in mtval3 is lost across suspend/resume cycles, and the stale mtval3 value after resume points to a wrong or invalid address
security_spec.summary: HSM suspend/resume CSR save/restore path must include mtval3 to preserve deferred async tag-mismatch fault address when M-mode memory tagging is active

findings.finding: HSM non-retentive suspend save path saves MIE, MIP, MEDELEG, MIDELEG, and MENVCFG but does not save mtval3. The mtval3 CSR (part of the proposed Zimt memory-tagging extension, CSR address not yet assigned in the ratified spec) holds the faulting virtual address for tag mismatches in M-mode. When/if Zimt is ratified and mseccfg.MT_MODE enables M-mode memory tagging, a tag-mismatch faulting address in mtval3 would be lost across non-retentive suspend/resume cycles, causing the stale mtval3 value after warm-boot resume to point to a wrong or invalid address. Neither CSR_MTVAL3 nor MSECCFG.MT_MODE are defined in OpenSBI's riscv_encoding.h.

spec_citations.excerpt: Zimt extension extends privileged specification with stval2, htval2 and mtval3 CSR to S, H and M mode respectively. On a tag mismatch and subsequent trap (asynchronous or synchronous mode), respective CSR holds the virtual address resulting in tag mismatch.

findings.finding: HSM non-retentive suspend restore path in sbi_hsm_hart_resume_finish restores MENVCFG, MIDELEG, MEDELEG, MIE, and MIP but does not restore mtval3. When the hart resumes from non-retentive suspend, the mtval3 CSR is left in its hardware-reset state (likely 0) rather than the pre-suspend tag-mismatch faulting address. If mseccfg.MT_MODE was non-zero before suspend and a tag mismatch was pending or had been captured in mtval3, that address information is irrecoverably lost. The sbi_hsm_data struct (lines 44-53) has no saved_mtval3 field.

spec_citations.excerpt: Zimt extension extends privileged specification with stval2, htval2 and mtval3 CSR to S, H and M mode respectively. On a tag mismatch and subsequent trap (asynchronous or synchronous mode), respective CSR holds the virtual address resulting in tag mismatch.

findings.finding: OpenSBI's CSR encoding header defines CSR_MTVAL (0x343) and CSR_MTVAL2 (0x34b) but does not define CSR_MTVAL3. There is also no MSECCFG_MT_MODE or MSECCFG_MT_ASYNC field definition in the mseccfg register block (lines 727-740), which only defines MML, MMWP, RLB, USEED, and SSEED. The RISC-V memory tagging (Zimt) extension is not yet ratified and OpenSBI has no awareness of it.

spec_citations.excerpt: In asynchronous mode, tag mismatch reporting can happen on any trap (exception or interrupt). This change adds additional CSR which can hold address which resulted in tag mismatch. Furthermore if sw check exception is being delivered due to tag mismatch, then also stval2/htval2/mtval3 CSR holds virtual address resulting in tag mismatch.
